newsitem.title: PERU: PERU'S UCP BACKUS BREWERY DENIES UNFAIR PRACTICE.
newsitem.headline: PERU'S UCP BACKUS BREWERY DENIES UNFAIR PRACTICE.

text.p: Peru's largest brewer, UCP Backus, denied a claim of unfair practice by its primary rival Cervesur, saying workers at a subsidiary distributor left Cervesur beer in the sun without management's knowledge.
Those workers "have infringed the policies of the distributor without the knowledge or authorization of its directors," Backus said in a statement.
The Backus-owned distributor, Distribuidora del Norte SA, delivers both Backus and Cervesur beer in the northern Lambayeque region.

Cervesur had claimed Tuesday that Backus deliberately kept Cervesur's beer in the sun before sale in order to harm its image among consumers. Cervesur has presented its charges -- involving about 1,000 liters of beer -- to the courts, where an official investigation has been opened, company spokesman Agustmn Valencia said.

But Backus countered: "It has been, is and will be the invariable policy of Backus to compete in the market with honesty ... the leadership of our company and of its products is not due to events like this that they try to unduly attribute to us."
Based on its strong presence in the south, Cervesur has a 20 percent share of Peruvian beer sales. Recently, it has made an aggressive push to eat into Backus's dominance in the north.

At the beginning of the year, the Backus group formed UCP Backus by merging its sister companies Backus y Johnston, Compaqma Nacional de Cerveza, Sociedad Cervecera de Trujillo and Cervecerma del Norte. The new company's full name is Unisn de Cervecermas Peruanas Backus y Johnston SA.
